translation_en: Qabisah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I visited the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, during his illness and touched him while he was suffering a severe fever. I said: You are suffering a severe fever, and that is because you will have a double reward. He said: “Yes. No Muslim is afflicted by harm except that his sins fall away from him as leaves fall from a tree.”

Ishaq narrated to us; Khalid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Khalid, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, visited a man who was ill and said: “No harm; it will be a purification, if Allah wills.” The man replied: “No! It is a fever boiling in an old man, destined to bring him to the graves.” The Prophet said: “Then so be it.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to me; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, that Usamah ibn Zayd informed him: Before the Battle of Badr, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, rode a donkey with a saddle covered by a Fadaki cloak, and seated Usamah behind him as he went to visit Sad ibn Ubadah. He continued until he passed a gathering that included Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, before Abdullah had accepted Islam. The gathering contained Muslims, polytheists who worshipped idols, and Jews; Abdullah ibn Rawahah was also there. When dust from the animal reached the gathering, Abdullah ibn Ubayy covered his nose with his cloak and said: “Do not disturb us.” The Prophet greeted them, stopped, dismounted, and invited them to Allah, reciting the Quran to them. Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: “Man, nothing is better than what you say if it is true, but do not disturb us with it in our gathering. Return to your mount, and whoever comes to you, tell it to him.” Ibn Rawahah said: “Yes, Messenger of Allah, bring it to us in our gatherings, for we love that.” The Muslims, polytheists, and Jews began arguing with one another until they nearly came to blows. The Prophet continued speaking until they fell silent. He mounted his animal and went to Sad ibn Ubadah. He said to him: “Sad, did you hear what Abu Hubab said?” meaning Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Sad said: “Messenger of Allah, pardon him and be patient with him. Allah has given you what He has given you. The people of this settlement had gathered to crown and make him their chief, but when the truth Allah gave you came and prevented that, he was distressed. That is why he acted as you saw.”

Amr ibn Abbas narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad—Ibn al-Munkadir—from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to visit me, not riding a mule or a fine-bred horse.

Qabisah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih and Ayyub, from Mujahid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Kab ibn Ujrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by me while I was tending a fire beneath a cooking pot. He said: “Are the lice on your head bothering you?” I said: “Yes.” He called for a barber, who shaved my head, then he ordered me to make an expiation.

Yahya ibn Yahya Abu Zakariyya narrated to us; Sulayman ibn Bilal informed us, from Yahya ibn Said, who said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: Aishah said, “Oh, my head!” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “That would be so if it happened while I was alive; I would ask forgiveness for you and pray for you.” Aishah said: “Oh, my loss! By Allah, I think you want me to die, so that you could spend the rest of your day with one of your other wives.” The Prophet said: “Rather, I have a headache too. I had intended—or wanted—to send for Abu Bakr and his son and make a bequest, lest someone make claims or wishful demands. Then I said: Allah will refuse it, and the believers will prevent it—or Allah will prevent it, and the believers will refuse it.”

Musa narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim narrated to us; Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Masud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I visited the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was suffering fever. I touched him and said: You are suffering a severe fever. He said: “Yes, as severely as two men among you.” I said: You will have a double reward? He said: “Yes. No Muslim is afflicted by harm, illness, or anything else except that Allah removes his sins as a tree sheds its leaves.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us; al-Zuhri informed us, from Amir ibn Sad, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to visit me because of an illness that had become severe during the Farewell Pilgrimage. I said: My illness has reached this state, and I have wealth, but only one daughter will inherit from me. May I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity? He said: “No.” I said: Half? He said: “No.” I said: A third? He said: “A third is a lot. It is better for you to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them dependent, begging from people. Whatever you spend seeking Allah's pleasure will be rewarded, even what you place in your wife's mouth.”

Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us; Hisham narrated to us, from Mamar. Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to me; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was near death, there were men in the house, including Umar ibn al-Khattab. The Prophet said: “Come, let me write for you a document after which you will not go astray.” Umar said: “The Prophet has been overcome by pain, and you have the Quran. The Book of Allah is enough for us.” The people in the house disagreed and argued. Some said: “Bring writing materials so the Prophet can write a document for you after which you will not go astray.” Others said what Umar had said. When they argued and spoke loudly in the Prophet's presence, the Messenger of Allah said: “Get up and leave.” Ubaydullah said: Ibn Abbas used to say: “The greatest calamity was that their disagreement and noise came between the Messenger of Allah and writing that document for them.”

Ibrahim ibn Hamzah narrated to us; Hatim—Ibn Ismail—informed us, from al-Juayd, who said: I heard al-Saib say: My maternal aunt took me to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “Messenger of Allah, my sister's son is ill.” He wiped my head and prayed for blessing for me, then performed ablution. I drank from the water of his ablution and stood behind him, where I saw the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders, like the button of a bridal canopy.

Adam narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us; Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Let none of you wish for death because of a hardship that has befallen him. If he must do so, let him say: O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is better for me, and let me die when death is better for me.”

Adam narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: We visited Khabbab while he was ill; he had been cauterized seven times. He said: Our companions who came before us have passed away without the world diminishing their reward. We have acquired wealth for which we find no place but the soil. Were it not that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade us to pray for death, I would have prayed for it. Then we visited him another time while he was building a wall for himself. He said: A Muslim is rewarded for everything he spends, except for what he puts into this soil.

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Ubayd, the freedman of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, informed me that Abu Hurairah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “No one's deeds alone will admit him to Paradise.” They said: “Not even you, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Not even me, unless Allah envelops me in His bounty and mercy. So act rightly and aim for what is close to perfection. Let none of you wish for death: if he is doing good, perhaps he will increase in good; and if he is doing wrong, perhaps he will seek to make amends.”

Abdullah ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from Abbad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: I heard Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, say: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was leaning against me, say: “O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and join me with the Highest Companion.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Masruq, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her: Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, visited a sick person—or a sick person was brought to him—he would say: “Remove the suffering, Lord of mankind; heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing except Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness behind.” Amr ibn Abi Qays and Ibrahim ibn Tahman reported from Mansur, from Ibrahim and Abu al-Duha: when the sick person was brought to him. Jarir reported from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha alone, who said: when he visited a sick person.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Ghundar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to me while I was ill, performed ablution, and poured the water over me—or he said: “Pour it over him.” I regained my senses and said: I will be inherited from only by distant relatives; how will the inheritance be divided? Then the verse of inheritance was revealed.

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived, Abu Bakr and Bilal became ill with fever. I went in to them and said: “Father, how are you feeling? Bilal, how are you feeling?” When Abu Bakr was overcome by fever, he would say: “Every man wakes among his family, while death is nearer to him than his sandal strap.” When Bilal's fever subsided, he would raise his voice and say: “Would that I knew whether I will spend a night in a valley, with idhkhir and jalil grasses around me; whether I will one day reach the waters of Majannah; and whether Shamah and Tufayl will appear to me.” Aishah said: I went to the Messenger of Allah and told him. He said: “O Allah, make Medina as beloved to us as Mecca, or even more; make it healthy for us, bless its sa and mudd, and move its fever to al-Juhfah.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us; Umar ibn Said ibn Abi Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ata ibn Abi Rabah narrated to me, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Allah has not sent down any disease without also sending down a cure for it.”

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us; Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Dhakwan, from Rubayyi bint Muawwidh ibn Afra, who said: We went on military expeditions with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. We gave the people water, served them, and took the dead and wounded back to Medina.

Al-Husayn narrated to me; Ahmad ibn Mani narrated to us; Marwan ibn Shuja narrated to us; Salim al-Aftas narrated to us, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: “Healing is in three things: a drink of honey, a cut made by cupping, and cauterization with fire. I forbid my community from cauterization.” He attributed the report to the Prophet. Al-Qummi reported it from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet, regarding honey and cupping.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to me; Surayj ibn Yunus Abu al-Harith informed us; Marwan ibn Shuja narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Healing is in three things: the incision of cupping, a drink of honey, or cauterization with fire. I forbid my community from cauterization.”

Abu Nuaim narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil narrated to us, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “If there is good in any of your remedies—or if there can be good in any of your remedies—it is in the incision of cupping, a drink of honey, or a cauterizing touch with fire that matches the illness. I do not like to be cauterized.”

Ayyash ibn al-Walid narrated to us; Abd al-Ala narrated to us; Said narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Abu Said: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “My brother is suffering from his stomach.” He said: “Give him honey to drink.” The man came a second time, and he said: “Give him honey to drink.” Then he came again and said: “I have done so.” He said: “Allah has spoken the truth, but your brother's stomach has lied. Give him honey to drink.” So he gave it to him, and he recovered.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Sallam ibn Miskin narrated to us; Thabit narrated to us, from Anas: Some people were ill and said: “Messenger of Allah, give us shelter and food.” When they recovered, they said: “The climate of Medina does not suit us.” He lodged them in the open rocky outskirts with some camels and said: “Drink their milk.” When they recovered, they killed the Prophet's shepherd and drove off the camels. He sent people after them, who caught them; he had their hands and feet cut off and their eyes branded. I saw one of them bite the ground with his tongue until he died. Sallam said: I heard that al-Hajjaj said to Anas: “Tell me about the harshest punishment the Prophet inflicted.” Anas told him this account. When al-Hasan heard of it, he said: “I wish he had not told him this.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: Some people found Medina's climate disagreeable, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered them to join the camel herder and drink the camels' milk and urine. They joined the herder and drank from their milk and urine until their bodies recovered. Then they killed the herder and drove off the camels. When news reached the Prophet, he sent people to pursue them. They were brought back, and he had their hands and feet cut off and their eyes branded. Qatadah said: Muhammad ibn Sirin told me that this happened before the legal punishments were revealed.

Abdullah ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; Ubaydullah narrated to us; Israil narrated to us, from Mansur, from Khalid ibn Sad, who said: We set out with us was Ghalib ibn Abjar, and he became ill on the road. We arrived in Medina while he was ill, and Ibn Abi Atiq visited him. He said to us: “Use this black seed. Take five or seven of them, crush them, then put drops of oil into the nostrils on both sides. Aishah told me that she heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: ‘This black seed is a cure for every illness except death.’” I asked: “What is death?” He said: “Death.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Salamah and Said ibn al-Musayyab informed me that Abu Hurairah informed them that he heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “In the black seed there is a cure for every illness except death.” Ibn Shihab said: Death means dying, and the black seed is shuniz.

Hibban ibn Musa informed us; Abdullah informed us; Yunus ibn Yazid informed us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she used to recommend talbinah for the sick and for those grieving a deceased person. She used to say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Talbinah comforts the heart of the sick person and relieves some of the grief.”
Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra narrated to us; Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, who used to recommend talbinah and say: “It is disliked but beneficial.”

Mual la ibn Asad narrated to us; Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had cupping performed, paid the cupper, and used nasal medication.
